commitments.quote: Basis our strong H1 FY27 financial performance. We raised our profitability guidance for FY27, ROA of 5.2% to 5.8% versus 4% to 4.8% earlier and ROE of 21% to 24% versus 16% to 20% earlier.
Basis our strong H1 FY27 financial performance. We raised our profitability guidance for FY27, ROA of 5.2% to 5.8% versus 4% to 4.8% earlier and ROE of 21% to 24% versus 16% to 20% earlier.
We retain our AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25%, supported by return to growth in Group Loan portfolio, coupled with continued momentum in Retail Finance.

We expect a NIM of 14.4% to 14.7% as against 12.8% to 13.2% guided earlier, driven by healthy asset quality, strong control over borrowing costs and a higher capital position even after factoring the 50-bps rate reduction applicable from October onwards.
Cost to income may range between 29% to 30% as operating costs remain well under control, despite inflationary trends.
We're maintaining our credit cost guidance of 3% to 4%, and it should comfortably cover for any volatility on account of evolving drought-related conditions in some operating geographies.

claims.claim: Reported highest quarterly profit of INR 502 Crore in Q2 FY27.
claims.quote: We reported our highest quarterly profit of INR 502 Crore in this quarter, having grown fivefold over the past 5 years.

claims.claim: Gross NPA improved to 1.79% and net NPA to 0.59%.
claims.quote: Gross NPA stood at 1.79%, net NPA at 0.59% and PAR 90 plus at 1.11%, each improving sequentially.

claims.claim: NIM expanded to 15.1% in Q2 from 14.4% in Q1.
claims.quote: We saw our NIM expand to 15.1% in Q2 from 14.4% in Q1, driven by lower interest reversals in Group Loan book, higher yielding individual loan book, stable cost of borrowing and higher capital push.

claims.claim: AUM grew 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ to INR 30,946 Crore.
claims.quote: Our AUM grew 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ to INR 30,946 Crore.

claims.claim: Borrower retention rates improved from 85% in FY26 to 88% in H1 FY27.
claims.quote: Further, our ability to meet evolving credit needs of our customers is also deepening their loyalty with borrower retention rates improving from 85% in FY26 to 88% in H1 FY27.

claims.claim: Temporary increase in PAR accretion in Aug-Sept due to excess rainfall and floods.
claims.quote: We saw a temporary increase in monthly PAR accretion rate during August and September, driven by excess rainfall and flooding in certain regions of Bihar, UP, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, along with seasonal festivities in a few geographies.

analyst_concerns.question: What is the extent of the portfolio exposed to drought-impacted districts in Maharashtra?
analyst_concerns.quote: What portion of portfolio will be coming from these districts approximately?

analyst_concerns.question: Why is borrower growth in single digits while AUM grows?
analyst_concerns.quote: My question was about your borrower growth. That seems to be in single digit. Is it that you are not acquiring new customers? Is that the problem that you are seeing for the entire micro industry?

analyst_concerns.question: What steps are being taken to combat customer attrition and concentration risk?
analyst_concerns.quote: Just firstly, what steps are we taking to combat this attrition? Do we have any structural advantage? Or are we going to keep competing against lower rate lenders and lose customers in the future?

commitments.target: Medium-term guidance of INR 50,000 Crore AUM by calendar year 2028
commitments.quote: We remain fully committed to our medium-term guidance of INR 50,000 Crore AUM by calendar year 2028, confidence reinforced by the strength of the start we have made this quarter across borrower additions, asset quality and margins.
commitments.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

claims.claim: Our AUM grew 16.4% YoY and 2.5% QoQ to INR 30,319 Crore.
claims.quote: Our AUM grew 16.4% YoY and 2.5% QoQ to INR 30,319 Crore, despite 6.3% TTM write-off and typical seasonal softness that Q1 brings.

claims.claim: Added 2.5 Lakh new borrowers during the quarter, with 35% new-to-credit.
claims.quote: We added 2.5 Lakh new borrowers during the quarter, of which 35% were new-to-credit, and we expect this run rate to improve further, adding close to an average of 1 Lakh borrowers per month going forward.

claims.claim: Retail finance book constitutes 20.6% of AUM, up 250 bps sequentially.
claims.quote: We continue to see the scale-up of our retail finance book, which now constitutes 20.6% of the AUM, up 250 bps sequentially from 18.1% in Q4 FY26.

claims.claim: Gross NPA stood at 2.18%, net NPA at 0.76% and PAR 90 at 1.46%.
claims.quote: Gross NPA stood at 2.18%, net NPA at 0.76% and PAR 90 at 1.46%, each showing sequential improvement.

claims.claim: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 720% YoY to INR 493 Crore with ROA of 5.9% and ROE of 24.4%.
claims.quote: As a result, our Q1 FY27 PAT grew 720% YoY to INR 493 Crore, resulting in an ROA of 5.9% and ROE of 24.4%.

claims.claim: Employee attrition moderated meaningfully to 20.6% in Q1 FY27 from 25.8% in Q1 FY26.
claims.quote: And importantly, employee attrition continued to moderate meaningfully, standing at 20.6% as of Q1 FY27 against 25.8% in Q1 FY26.

analyst_concerns.question: Do you foresee any risk to current strong momentum due to El Nino or war?
analyst_concerns.quote: So first on the guidance part, right? So do you foresee any risk to, let's say, current strong momentum maybe due to El Nino, second order impact of war, etcetera? And hence, we are not changing guidance or we might revisit in Q2?

analyst_concerns.question: What is the timeline for new retail products to generate steady-state ROAs and ROEs?
analyst_concerns.quote: And is there any time line in management's mind, for example, let's say, mortgage, you get in the business for more than 2 years. And what could be the time frame wherein the new business should start generating steady-state ROAs or ROEs?

analyst_concerns.question: What kind of pricing reduction will happen in H2 given the high ROE in Q1?
analyst_concerns.quote: See, I just wanted to understand what kind of pricing reduction will have to happen in the second half if the current collection trends continue? Because I think there is a big disconnect between the ROE you've delivered in the first quarter and for the whole year guidance, you've retained it. Then what kind of pricing reduction will have to happen?

analyst_concerns.question: How cushioned is the 3% to 4% credit cost guidance given lower annualized rates and write-offs?
analyst_concerns.quote: And Nilesh, even in the credit cost, right, I mean, this quarter, it annualized 2.8%, but you still have write-off-related credit costs.

claims.claim: The AUM grew 14.0% YoY and 11.4% QoQ, in line with annual guidance, despite 7.6% write-offs made in FY26.
claims.quote: The AUM grew 14.0% YoY and 11.4% QoQ, in line with the annual growth guidance, despite 7.6% write-offs made in FY26.

claims.claim: NIMs expanded by 35 bps QoQ to 14.2% in Q4.
claims.quote: NIMs expanded by 35 bps QoQ to 14.2% in Q4.

claims.claim: Cost of borrowing further declined to 9.2% in Q4, marking a total 60 bps reduction during the year.
claims.quote: Cost of borrowing further declined to 9.2% in Q4, marking a total 60 bps reduction during the year.

claims.claim: PAT grew over 6x YoY and 34.7% QoQ to INR 340 Crore, translating to an ROA of 4.4% and an ROE of 17.8%.
claims.quote: PAT grew over 6x YoY and 34.7% QoQ to INR 340 Crore, translating to an ROA of 4.4% and an ROE of 17.8%.

claims.claim: Credit cost ended at 6.74% as against the guidance of 5.5% to 6.0% due to new PAR and ECL rate increases.
claims.quote: our credit cost ended at 6.74% as against the guidance of 5.5% to 6.0%. The 6.74% credit cost consisted of 6.10% due to new PAR and 0.64% due to increase in ECL provisioning rates.

claims.claim: Added 3.3 Lakh borrowers in Q4 and 9.8 Lakh borrowers in FY26, with 38% being new to credit.
claims.quote: We continue to scale borrower acquisition with 3.3 Lakh borrowers added in Q4, while 9.8 Lakh borrowers added in FY26, of which 38% were new to credit.

analyst_concerns.question: Why such a wide band in terms of the credit cost guidance of 3.0-4.0%?
analyst_concerns.quote: Just trying to understand this time around why such a wide band in terms of the credit cost guidance 3.0-4.0%. And within this, as per your estimates, what proportion of this could be because of the higher ECL provision?

analyst_concerns.question: Are we on the conservative side with credit cost guidance given lower PAR accretion rates?
analyst_concerns.quote: our PAR accretion rates are much lower than what we've seen in the past in the last few quarters. And you know, it's under 10 bps; we are 13 plus. But still, we have given like 3-4% kind of a guidance in credit cost. Like, are we on the conservative side here just to be on the safer side? Even with the geopolitical crisis, I know, the credit cost could be under 3%?

analyst_concerns.question: Why is the guided NIM lower than the exit NIM of 14.2%?
analyst_concerns.quote: And on NIMs, when I look at your guided NIM, the midpoint is 13%, you are exiting at 14.2%. I know there will be a leveraging effect because of growth. But still, I mean, the kind of NIM decline that we are trying to indicate in the guidance, is it because of the change in mix, which I don't believe is so diluted, but is it because of cost of fund changes that you are indicating? Or are you planning to pass on incremental hand strength and efficiencies by reducing pricing?

analyst_concerns.question: Does the cost-to-income guidance suggest that costs will grow higher than income?
analyst_concerns.quote: And we were thinking that when the growth will come back, you will also have some operating efficiencies, which you're trying to pass through pricing. But when I look at cost-to-income guidance, it seems to suggest that your cost will grow higher than income?

commitments.target: FY27 credit cost guidance of 4% to 4.5%
commitments.quote: Our FY27 credit cost guidance of 4% to 4.5% reflects a new PAR 15 accretion rate of 30-35 bps per month.
commitments.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

commitments.target: Medium-term foreign borrowings target of 25-30% by FY28

claims.claim: X bucket collection efficiency stood at 99.71% in December 2025.
claims.quote: Our X bucket collection efficiency stood at 99.71% in December 2025, while monthly PAR 15+ accretion declined sharply to 18 bps in December 2025 from 47 bps in September 2025.

claims.claim: Q3 FY26 disbursements grew 13.4% YoY to INR 5,767 Crore.
claims.quote: The disbursements for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 5,767 Crore, increasing by 13.4% YoY with the exit month December crossing INR 2,200 Crore mark.

claims.claim: Average cost of borrowings declined 26 bps QoQ to 9.4%.
claims.quote: Our average cost of borrowings continues to trend lower, reflecting disciplined liability management, having declined 26 bps QoQ to 9.4% at the end of Q3 FY26.

claims.claim: Net interest income grew 13.4% YoY to INR 977 Crore.
claims.quote: Net interest income grew 13.4% YoY to INR 977 Crore with portfolio yield of 21.0% versus 20.7% in Q2 FY26.

claims.claim: PAT doubled QoQ to INR 252 Crore in Q3 FY26.
claims.quote: PAT doubled QoQ to INR 252 Crore, while adjusted figures stood at INR 266 Crore, translating to an ROA and ROE of 3.5% and 13.8%, respectively.

claims.claim: NIM increased by 60 bps QoQ to 13.9% in Q3 FY26.
claims.quote: NIM increased by 60 bps QoQ to 13.9% in Q3 FY26.

analyst_concerns.question: How is Karnataka seeing recovery when other non-MFI lenders report disturbed credit discipline?
analyst_concerns.quote: While you guys have reported great numbers, some of the non-MFI lenders commentary earlier this quarter or maybe even closer to December was that the credit discipline in Karnataka state, which got disturbed after the MFI ordinance came into place, which impacted our retail loans also is still not back.

analyst_concerns.question: Are bank lines drying up or becoming more expensive for NBFC-MFIs?
analyst_concerns.quote: Even if the lines are available, they are coming at a significantly higher cost of funds. So, if you can speak to us about the -- any challenges or any areas that we are struggling with our bank borrowings or our bank relationships.

analyst_concerns.question: How have rejection rates trended after the implementation of MFIN guardrails?
analyst_concerns.quote: Sir, first thing on the industry, most other players talk about a very high rejection rate today, especially after the implementation of MFIN guardrails. So, if you could just help us understand how have our rejection rates trended over the last maybe 2, 3 quarters?

annual.what_it_does: CreditAccess Grameen is India's largest NBFC-MFI, empowering women entrepreneurs and low-income households with flexible financial solutions. It offers inclusive group loans, retail finance, micro-insurance, and holistic community support.

segments.name: Group Loans
segments.note: Includes various term loans like IGL, emergency, and sanitation loans

segments.name: Retail Loans
segments.note: Includes unsecured business, Vikas, Unnati, and two-wheeler loans

annual.customers: Women entrepreneurs and low-income households across rural and semi-urban India.

facts.fact: Assets Under Management reached J 295.90 billion with 4.42 million active borrowers.
Operating across 16 states and 1 union territory.
Total CSR spend of J 251.53 million supporting 392,518 beneficiaries.
Maintains 17,727 branch audits performed during the year.

annual.geography: Operates domestically across 16 states and 1 union territory in India, with 87% of the borrower base comprising rural customers.
annual.revenue_mix_basis: Not applicable as single operating segment reported.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic factors leading to higher inflation impacting borrower affordability.
Socio-political developments including localised unrest or election-related disruptions.
Attrition among frontline loan officers impacting productivity and relationship continuity.
Competitive intensity in mature markets and increasing reliance on digital platforms.

narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Jun 2026 PAT of INR 493.0 crore vs Jun 2025 PAT of INR 60.0 crore represents a 721.7% YoY increase.

bull.point: Q2 FY27 net profit reached a record INR 502 crore with operating profit margin expanding to 36.1%.
Management raised FY27 guidance across ROA to 5.2%-5.8% and ROE to 21%-24% following strong H1 performance.
5-year PAT CAGR stands at 42.8% and promoter holding remains strong at 63.83% as of Sep 2026.

bear.point: FY26 credit cost finished at 6.74%, missing initial guidance of 5.5%-6.0% due to asset quality slippages.
Cash flow from operations was negative at INR -2,770 crore in FY26, continuing a multi-year trend of operating cash deficits.
PAR accretion risks persist due to excess rainfall, floods in August-September, and drought conditions in Maharashtra.

watch.point: Impact of flood and drought conditions on H2 FY27 credit costs and PAR accretion.
NIM retention within 14.4%-14.7% target range following the October 50 bps interest rate reduction.
AUM growth momentum towards the full-year FY27 target of 20% to 25%.
